description: In a declarative frame, 'tho' ends the content introduced by 'tha' (DECL.COMP). The governing predicate follows; this audible boundary prevents its verb from being heard as part of the embedded statement.
articulatory_notes: The same dental breath opens the word: tongue tip at the backs of the upper teeth, unvoiced air escaping over it. Voice begins as the lips round and the tongue body draws back for mid 'o'. A single stressed syllable, and that rounding at the end is the whole audible difference from 'tha' (DECL.COMP).
usage_notes: After the subject, 'tha' opens the statement and 'tho' closes it before the matrix predicate. Its internal verb takes the tense appropriate to that statement. A pause never substitutes for 'tho', and nested pairs close from the inside out.

examples.phi: shia tha thia so kamo tho haolu.
examples.translation: They say that you will arrive.
